Maya R: ran a 4xA100 nsys+nccL capture on the repro branch (batching-handoff). attaching perfetto link and a short tl;dr: big token-level stall when we cross the 1024 token frontier, allreduce overlap drops off and one GPU goes idle for ~60ms.
Samir: can you paste the nvprof/nsys flame snippet? curious which kernels are sitting while NCCL is busy.
Maya R: gist of the hotspot:
```
Kernel timeline (GPU0): cudaLaunchKernel attention_fused_fp16  0.0-12.3ms
Kernel timeline (GPU0): cudaLaunchKernel matmul_fp16 12.4-14.0ms
NCCL allReduce start 14.1ms - 75.0ms
Kernel timeline (GPU0): cudaLaunchKernel prefetch_kv 75.2-75.6ms (short bursts)
```
Jin W: interesting — looks like the runtime selected the fp16 fused attention for early steps but falls back to an unfused matmul path right before allreduce. that extra 1.6ms push probably shifts the batch frontier and causes the NCCL scheduling skew.
Maya R: yes, binder shows kernel-selector switching at sequence length = 1024 boundary. selector config: `prefer_fused_when_tokens<=1024` — but when batching mixes short+long sequences, the heuristic triggers selector handoff mid-batch.
Samir: do we have KV cache access pattern traces? prefetch_kv spikes coincide with post-allreduce gap? could be cache thrash due to stride mismatch.
Maya R: I captured per-step KV load counts in the perf log: GPU2 shows 3x more `kv_get` misses during the gap window. seems like shift in key offsets after a failed prefetch handshake.
perf-bot: archived profile -> https://perf.redwood/profiles/2045123456 (nsys + perfetto stitched). flamegraph attached. :mag_right:
ops-bot: archived trace -> s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/2045/2045123456.tar.gz
Jin W: hypothesis: kernel-selector uses sequence-length quantization binning that's too coarse. mixing sequences with padless packing causes per-GPU variance in effective token counts which pushes one device over the bin edge. selector chooses unfused kernel that elongates compute and desyncs NCCL schedule.
Samir: sounds plausible. quick test: force kernel selection to fused for all lengths and re-run the capture; if overlap improves then selector is culprit. can we hotfix a runtime flag?
Maya R: yes can set `FORCE_FUSED_ATTENTION=1` in the runtime and re-run. I'll spin a run with NVTX markers and a reduced workload (batch size 8, 4 devices) to keep trace size small.
Jin W: also add an nvprof counter for DRAM bw and L2 hit rate around the KV slot region, want to see if prefetch is causing L2 eviction cascade.
Maya R: good call. after that, if fused fixes it, we should tighten the quantization bins and change handoff to per-subbatch decision instead of full-batch.
Samir: and add a short-lived telemetry metric: `kernel_selector_fallback_rate` + token-length histogram so we can correlate in prod without full traces.
perf-bot: scheduled follow-up capture template: `nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda,nccl --sample=cpu --output=2045123456-handoff`
Maya R: re-run queued. will post results in this thread. next steps: 1) re-run with FORCE_FUSED_ATTENTION, NVTX markers, L2 counters 2) collect KV miss stats + token hist 3) if fixed, submit selector-binning PR + telemetry.
Samir: awesome, thanks. ping me when trace uploaded. :thumbsup:
